Subject: Post-demo — clarifying concurrency and streaming needs

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can finish scoping: 

- Target: integrate generative assistant into our trader desk UI for short-form summarization and streaming transcripts of market events.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency under 150ms for non-streaming completions; for streaming we need tokens emitted within 100ms of availability (low tail).
- Throughput: steady-state 600 concurrent active users during market hours, peak bursts up to ~2,500 concurrent sessions for short windows (2–5 minutes) around open/close.
- Concurrency model: our client opens a WebSocket per session and multiplexes 2 parallel requests per session for background summarization + active streaming.

Can you confirm how Redwood would map this into connection pool sizes / parallel-request quotas and any recommended rate limits? Also — do you have a suggested fallback model if we exceed reserved capacity (e.g., degrade to shorter summaries or reduce parallel background requests)?

Samir
Head of Product, Vertex Financial

Samir / Monica — feeding in a technical sizing and options doc. High level answers first, then sizing assumptions.

High-level mapping:
- Effective parallel requests = sessions * parallel_requests_per_session (you noted 2). For 600 steady-state => 1,200 concurrent requests; peak 2,500 => 5,000 concurrent requests.
- Connection pool: we recommend reserving socket slots equal to steady-state concurrent requests plus a burst reserve. For your pattern we suggest: reserved pool = 1,500, burst pool = additional 3,500 (fast-burst capacity) with automated short-term billing for bursts.
- Rate limits / quotas: enforce token-rate limits per connection and per-API-key. We propose per-connection QPS limit of 20 requests/sec and per-tenant quota mapped to reserved + burst windows.
- Streaming: to hit the 100ms emit target, configure small continuous-batching (max batch latency 25ms) and keep KV cache warm on the same node group. Streaming sessions are prioritized in the routing policy during bursts.

Sizing assumptions (please confirm):
- Streaming sessions = 55% of active sessions. Average streaming token output = 40 tokens/minute/session (low-volume, frequent tokens).
- Non-streaming completions: avg 250 tokens per request, avg 1 completion per session every 10 minutes.
- Tail safety factor: 1.8x capacity to keep 95th latency under target at 99% load.

Based on those numbers:
- Steady-state parallelism: ~1,320 concurrent reqs (600 * 2 * 1.1 safety), provisioned as reserved capacity.
- Peak hard cap (5-minute window): ~6,500 concurrent reqs to absorb bursts with safety factor and background retransmits.
- Suggested quota plan: Reserved quota for RWD-2391 = 1,500 connections / 3,000 concurrent request slots; Burst add-on = up to 6,000 extra slots with short-term billing and pre-warm API to avoid cold-start penalties.

Fallback policy options we recommend (pick one):
A) Priority degrade: prioritize streaming tokens and degrade non-streaming background summarization (reduce to 1 background request per session).
B) Quality degrade: serve shorter summaries (cut completion length by 30%) when burst threshold hit.
C) Regional failover: route excess traffic to a secondary region with looser latency SLOs (if acceptable from compliance perspective).

I'll attach a CSV with a few example traffic curves and a sample ratecard. If these assumptions look right I can convert to a formal proposal and SLA addendum.

- Rishi
Senior Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

- Token rate for streaming: closer to 60 tokens/minute/session during high-volatility windows.

Samir / Alex — thanks, team. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

What we heard:
- Steady-state: 600 active sessions, 70% streaming during market hours; average streaming token output up to 60 tokens/minute when volatile.
- Peak bursts: up to ~2,500 sessions, implies ~5,000 parallel requests; you want a short 3–5 minute burst window around open/close.
- Compliance: regional failover is off the table.

Our proposal (attached):
- Reserved tier: 1,800 connection slots / 3,600 concurrent request capacity to cover steady-state + 20% headroom.
- Burst pack: 6-minute elastic burst allowance up to +6,000 concurrent slots (metered by-minute with pre-warm API).
- Routing & priorities: streaming tokens prioritized during bursts; non-streaming background summarization will be reduced to single background request when threshold exceeded (your preferred A).
- Estimated cost impact: typical week (two scheduled bursts per day for open/close): ~ +12% on monthly committed spend. Extreme event day (sustained 30% higher sessions for the day): ~ +65% incremental for that day, billed as metered burst usage.

Next steps / action items:
1) Vertex: confirm streaming percentage and token rate (Alex to share anonymized minute-level sample CSV if possible).
2) Redwood (Rishi): produce final CSV with traffic curves and a 1-page SLA addendum draft.
